name: Til Kumari Sharma

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Til Kumari Sharma is a poet from Hile in Parbat, Nepal, also known as Pushpa. Her poems appear in international literary publications, including Inner Child Press’s “The Year of the Poet”. Alongside creative writing, she has written about English literature; a published study examines spiritual crisis in T. S. Eliot’s “The Waste Land”.

In “Shining Statue of Mine”, writing becomes the means of making a self that cannot be defined by the crowd. The solitary moon, a ladder of light and the repeated image of carving a statue give artistic work a visible form. The speaker’s words build both an identity and an ethical claim: solitude is difficult, but it can also become a source of illumination for others.
